torque-angle-work.alt: Left: a hand pushes up on the handle of a crank wheel, turning it counterclockwise through an angle Δθ; for a constant torque, the work is W = τΔθ, with the angle in radians and work in joules. Right: a graph of torque in N·m against angle in radians. The torque is 4.0 N·m from 0 to 10 rad, then falls in a straight line to zero at 20 rad and stays zero. The shaded area under the line is the work: a rectangle of 4.0 × 10 = 40 J plus a triangle of ½ × 4.0 × 10 = 20 J, 60 J in all.
